source.title: Dynamic Jailbreaking Attack
source.authors: Kedong Xiu; Yun-Han Yang; Churui Zeng; Tian-Hang Zheng; Xinzhe Huang; Di Wang; Pu-Ning Zhao; Zhan Qin; Kui Ren

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether adversarial suffix attacks can elicit harmful compliance, using a dynamic gradient-based attack and behavioral success rates; it does not reproduce fine-tuning or measure token-position KL.
record.gate_note: The study tests suffix-based jailbreak attacks and reports attack success rates, so it bears on V4. It does not test harmful or benign fine-tuning, aligned-versus-base KL by response position, compliant-token prefilling, safety localization in weights, why safety is shallow, or training that deepens safety. Its candidate-sampling temperature sweep changes the attack's target-sampling setting, not the victim model's final-response decoding. Rows for response-quality profiles and cited results are omitted because they do not add a separate direct test of the versions recorded here.
record.test_reason: DJA is a gradient-based suffix attack, reported by attack success rate against 40 aligned models. V4 names suffixes as a way past refusal, so these results bear on it. Prefilling and decoding changes are not tested on the victim model.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly right. The authors conclude that static gradient-based attacks underestimate LLM vulnerability, and that dynamic targets plus adaptive effort reach 100% ASR on all 40 models. Attack cost varies with model and prompt. The record omits that the 100% rests on an unbounded round budget, while the comparators were capped at 300 iterations.
record.recipe_differences: Uses gradient-based adversarial suffix optimization with dynamically sampled targets and adaptive attack effort; it does not use fine-tuning, compliant-opening prefilling, or per-token KL analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: DJA candidate-sampling temperature changes reported ASR: 98% at 0.7, 95% at 1.0, 98% at 1.5, and 100% at 2.0, under a 30-round cap. Attack method and target model also correspond to different ASRs in the baseline comparison.
record.code_released: The paper says a package is provided in the supplementary material; no URL is stated.
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for ASR. The evaluation uses GPT-4o as the composite judge, with only a stated spot-check against manual judgment. The comparison benchmark uses 100 sampled prompts; the 40-model results report attack success without a no-suffix baseline. ASR depends on the study's composite success threshold and, in the temperature sweep, on the attack's candidate-sampling temperature.
record.rows_left_out: The 60-row limit was reached. Omitted the 15 defended-attack results in Table 5 (four baselines and DJA across Perplexity, SmoothLLM, and Paraphrase) and the five DJA model-specific values in Table 3; also omitted Table 3's average-ASR column. These are reported separately but were left out to retain the 40 individual large-scale model results, the varying baseline attack outcomes, and the sampling-temperature sweep.

untested.parts: No per-token KL between aligned and base models.
Prefilling a compliant start is not tested on the victim model. Changes to final-response decoding are not tested as a bypass; the sweep varies the attack's candidate sampling temperature instead.
No localization of safety in weights or ranks.
No test of why safety is shallow.

missing.what: No-suffix baseline refusal or ASR for the 40 models, so the size of the suffix effect cannot be read

Per-model attack cost (mean, median, max rounds, suffix length). It is the study's graded finding, as ASR is saturated at 100%, and is not recorded as rows. Examples: 64.96 mean rounds for GPT-OSS-20B and 55.61 for Qwen2.5-32B against 1.95 for Qwen2.5-0.5B.
Defended-attack ASR under Perplexity, SmoothLLM and Paraphrase (DJA 87-99%, baselines mostly under 12%). The rows_left_out note says these were omitted.

record.verdict_notes: The row-level 'partial' states on comparators are artifacts of a strict composite judge and a capped baseline budget. The V4 limits_scope verdict on the comparator rows (R41-R56) and the temperature-sweep rows (R57-R59) should be dropped. The 100% rows are all from one attack under one judge, and the study evaluates with a GPT-4o composite (threshold 0.6) and spot-checks only manually. Table 3 DJA values of 98-98.8% conflict with the 100% claim for four models, apparently because of the 30-round cap in that comparison. The instructions-in-text flag is unexplained; no injected instructions were followed.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples or measurement of refusal after fine-tuning.
No fine-tuning on benign data or measurement of resulting harmful compliance.
Tests adversarial suffix attacks; does not test prefilling a compliant opening or changing the victim model's final-response decoding.
No localization or editing of safety-related weights or ranks.
No test of whether training data or objective produces shallow safety.
No training to spread safety beyond initial tokens and no test of whether such training holds up.

relationships.condition: DJA adversarial suffixes (white-box, dynamic targets) on 40 open-weight models, AdvBench 100 prompts, composite GPT-4o criterion
relationships.reason: R01-R40 report 100% ASR on every model, including the hardest, GPT-OSS-20B (about 65 rounds on average). There is no no-suffix baseline and no uncertainty, so this shows suffixes can defeat refusal, not by how much.
relationships.display_finding: Attack success was 100% on every model, with GPT-OSS-20B the hardest at about 65 rounds on average, but without a no-suffix baseline or uncertainty this shows suffixes can defeat refusal, not by how much.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: DJA on the 40 models in Tables 1 and 2
reader_labels.reason: DJA reports 100% attack success on each listed model, showing suffix-based attacks elicited harmful, relevant completions under the study's composite criterion (R01–R40).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: GCG, I-GCG, COLD-Attack, and AdvPrefix on four compared models
reader_labels.reason: The comparator suffix attacks have incomplete and model-dependent ASRs, ranging from 13% to 89% in the reported model-method results (R41–R56).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: At the default candidate-sampling temperature the attack reaches 100% ASR within the 30-round cap (R60).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The reported ASRs are below 100% at these candidate-sampling temperatures, showing outcome sensitivity to this attack setting (R57–R59).
